first_impression.reaction: Googled 'best time to get married in bali' on the train. The first line says there's no single right time. Fine, but just tell me which months. Key Takeaways give me the wet season window and the Nyepi date, so I can work out 'May to September' myself, but nobody actually says it. I'd skim the month list and bookmark it. Not enquiring.

journey.quote: There is no single right time to get married in Bali.
journey.reaction: I searched 'best time' and the first thing I read is 'it depends'. A bit of a dodge.

journey.quote: Indonesia's wet season usually runs around October to April, when weather can change quickly and heavy rain can flood roads in Bali.
journey.reaction: OK, that's the real answer, and it's near the top. Wet October to April, so dry is the rest.

journey.quote: Nyepi falls on Monday 8 March 2027, beside the Idul Fitri holidays and collective leave, so ask your venue early how the day affects guests and suppliers.
journey.reaction: Specific 2027 date. Didn't know about this. Useful and current.

journey.section: What are Bali's dry and wet seasons?
journey.quote: The months outside that window, May to September, form the drier half of the year.
journey.reaction: This is the line I wanted, but it's in section one, not the first 100 words.

journey.quote: **July.** No national holidays or collective leave days fall in July 2027.
journey.reaction: Short and scannable on my phone. But the months are mostly about holidays, not what the weather is actually like. Is July sunny? Hot? Busy?

journey.quote: **March.** The month with the most to plan around.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: BMKG writes onset in dasarian: days 1 to 10, 11 to 20, and 21 to the end of the month.
journey.reaction: Way more detail than I need. Rainfall millimetre bands? I'm scrolling past.

journey.quote: The 2027 national holidays are 1 and 5 January, 6 February, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 28 March, 1, 6, 17 and 20 May, 1 and 6 June, 15 and 17 August, and 25 and 26 December.
journey.reaction: A wall of dates in one sentence. Already had these month by month. Hard to read on a phone.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Notice the capacities. A chapel for 70 and a lawn for 250 suit very different guest lists, and the covered space needs to hold everyone, not only the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Good point I wouldn't have thought of.

journey.quote: If the ceremony must be outdoors, the drier months outside the October to April window give you the most room.
journey.reaction: Finally a near-recommendation, but this far down I'd probably have left already.

journey.quote: No single month suits every wedding.
journey.reaction: FAQ is short and direct, which I like, but there's no 'what's the best month' question, which is literally what I typed.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
journey.reaction: Nice idea. AUD though, and I'm in Singapore. Not sure this is for me.

unanswered_questions: What's the single best month if I just want the best chance of sunshine for an outdoor ceremony?
What's the weather actually like month by month (heat, humidity, rain), not just the holidays?
Which months are peak tourist season, and do prices or availability change? (not on the page)
Do you work with couples who don't live in Australia or don't pay in AUD? (deferred business detail)
How much does Wedded Concierge cost? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: There is no single right time to get married in Bali.
turn_offs_found.why: Headline promises the best time but the opening dodges it; the plain 'May to September is drier' answer only appears in the first section, outside the first 100 words.

turn_offs_found.quote: BMKG writes onset in dasarian: days 1 to 10, 11 to 20, and 21 to the end of the month.
turn_offs_found.why: The forecast-reading section is technical detail a quick searcher doesn't need, and it pushes the 'which months suit you' answer and the FAQ further down.

turn_offs_found.quote: The 2027 national holidays are 1 and 5 January, 6 February, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 28 March, 1, 6, 17 and 20 May, 1 and 6 June, 15 and 17 August, and 25 and 26 December.
turn_offs_found.why: A single run-on list of dates repeats the month-by-month notes and is hard to scan on a phone.

would_share_with: My partner: a screenshot of the Key Takeaways and the March / Nyepi bit

cta_reaction.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, [talk to Wedded Concierge about your dates](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-bali&utm_content=primary) and turn them into dates a venue can hold.
cta_reaction.why: I'm just checking months, don't know the brand, and it quotes in AUD. Bookmark, not enquire.

top_3_changes: Put a plain answer in the first 100 words: May to September is the drier half and gives outdoor ceremonies the most room; October to April needs a covered plan.
Add a line or two of actual weather per month (or per season), not just the holiday dates, and an FAQ for 'What is the best month to get married in Bali?'.
Shorten or move the BMKG forecast section lower and turn the 2027 holiday sentence into a short list or drop it, since the months already cover it.
